fields.meta_description: Build a personal information form that collects contact details, reminds anyone who has not filed, and sends changes to HR. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Personal Information Form That Stays Current
fields.hero_description: Build a personal information form that keeps every record in a database you own and current as details change.
fields.features_heading: What the Form Collects and Where It Goes
fields.features_subheading: A personal information form records who someone is and how to reach them. These six parts decide how those details stay accurate.
fields.feature_1:
Fields named in your own words

Emergent builds the form from a plain-English list of fields, such as legal name, home address, and an emergency contact. Ask for another field later and Emergent adds it.
fields.feature_2:
One question per screen on a phone

The form can show one question at a time, which suits someone filling it in on a phone between shifts. Put the required details first and leave the optional ones for the end.
fields.feature_3:
Records in a database you own

Every submission is saved in a database you own, with one row per person and a column for each field. Search it by name when someone calls in to give a new phone number.
fields.feature_4:
Reminders for anyone who has not filed

The form sends an email or Slack reminder to each person who has not filed by your due date. People who already filed hear nothing, and the list of names shrinks each day.
fields.feature_5:
No cap on how many people respond

Emergent sets no response cap on forms. A 40-person school and a 600-person staffing pool run the same form, and nobody has to count submissions near the end of a month.
fields.feature_6:
Details sent to the tools you already use

A finished record can go to any tool with an API, such as HubSpot or a scheduling app. Nobody retypes an address, and your database keeps the full record either way.

fields.usecase_heading: Where the Details Go After Someone Files
fields.tab_content_1:
Teachers missing on August 12 get an email reminder

Linden Hollow Academy asks its 42 teachers to update their personal details before school starts, with a due date of August 15. On August 12, the office dashboard showed 39 filed. The 3 teachers still missing, Kasimir Dalby among them, got an email reminder that morning. Nobody who had filed heard a thing.
fields.tab_content_2:
HR signs off on every address change

Femi Okonjo, a driver at Calder Ridge Freight, moved in March and filed a change of address on his phone. HR coordinator Dorrit Haverly got an email with his old address, 14 Alder Court, next to the new one, 902 Birch Lane. She approved it. His record now shows Birch Lane, and Alder Court stays in its history.
fields.tab_content_3:
The office manager checks 6 of 120 scanned forms

Thistle Lane Senior Center had 120 paper forms from new participants. Staff scanned the stack, and 114 were read into records with every field filled. The other 6 had a handwritten date of birth that could not be read clearly. Those went to office manager Esperanza Imrie, who typed in each date from the paper.
fields.tab_content_4:
9 phone questions put a server into the scheduling app

Wexcombe Events keeps a pool of on-call servers for weddings and galas. Juno Akintola filled in the form on her phone, one question per screen, and finished all 9 questions. Her record went to the scheduling app the agency connected. Staffing lead Petra Lunde then booked her for Saturday's wedding.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Personal Information Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a personal information form that people finish on time and that stays accurate as details change.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List only the details you need
fields.howto_step_1_des: Write down each detail someone will act on, like a mailing address for paychecks or a phone number for shift changes. Leave out the rest, such as a Social Security number on a club roster.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Put identity fields first, contact details next, and the emergency contact last. Add a section only your group needs, such as the subject a teacher covers or a server's weekend availability.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Tell Emergent in a few sentences who fills in the form, which fields it holds, and when it is due. Emergent builds the form and the database that stores each record.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Mark which fields are required. Pick one date format, such as MM/DD/YYYY, so every date of birth reads the same way in the records.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Name who hears about each record
fields.howto_step_5_des: Say who gets a reminder after the due date and who approves a change, such as an HR coordinator. Name one person rather than a whole team.
fields.howto_step_6_des: List the tools that should receive each record, such as a scheduling app or HubSpot. Decide which fields each tool gets, so a scheduler sees availability but never a home address.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit a complete entry, an entry missing a required field, and a change to a record you already have. Confirm each one lands where you expect, then delete the test rows.

faq_plan.q: What is a personal information form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a personal information form?

prov.original: What is a personal information form?

faq_plan.a: A personal information form is a form that collects the details needed to identify and reach one person: legal name, date of birth, home address, phone, email, and an emergency contact. Keep one completed form per person, and treat it as that person's record.

faq_plan.q: How to make a personal information form?
faq_plan.ref: how to make a personal information form
faq_plan.a: Describe the form to Emergent's AI form builder in plain English, starting with who fills it in and what it asks for. Then say who should hear about a late or changed record. Emergent builds the form along with the database behind it. Fill in a few test entries yourself before you share the link.

faq_plan.q: What is the short form for personal information?
faq_plan.ref: What is the short form for personal information?

prov.original: What is the short form for personal information?

faq_plan.a: PII is the short form, from personally identifiable information. NIST's glossary uses PII for any detail that can point to one individual, by itself or when combined with other linked data. Treat the answers on personal information forms as PII, and limit who can open them to the people who need them.

faq_plan.q: How do I make a personal information form to send in an email?
faq_plan.ref: how to make a personal information form in e mail
faq_plan.a: Build the form online and paste its link into the email instead of attaching a document. Each person fills it in from the link, and the answers arrive as a record rather than a reply you have to retype. A rental application form goes out the same way: one link in the email and one record per applicant.

faq_plan.q: What should a teacher personal information form include?
faq_plan.a: A teacher personal information form should include what a school office needs to reach the teacher: legal name, home address, personal phone and email, and an emergency contact. Add the subjects and grades taught, plus each certification number and its expiration date if your office tracks them. Set the due date a week or more before the first day of classes.

faq_plan.q: What is a good personal information form format?
faq_plan.a: A good format is one column of labeled fields under three headings: about you, how to reach you, and who to call in an emergency. Give each part of an address its own box: street, city, state, and ZIP code. Mark required fields with an asterisk and keep optional ones at the bottom.

faq_plan.q: What does a personal information form sample include?
faq_plan.a: A personal information form sample includes a preferred name next to the legal name, a second emergency contact, and an optional line for medical notes. For a driver application form, keep those basics and add a license number and driving history. Describe your own version to Emergent and it builds a working form you can test before anyone else sees it.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free personal information form template?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing the form. Instead of editing a fixed personal information form template, you list the fields you want and get a form built around them.

faq_plan.q: What is a change of personal information form?
faq_plan.a: A change of personal information form updates details already on file, such as a new address, phone number, or legal name. Ask for the date the change takes effect. For a name change, ask for the new name exactly as it appears on the person's ID.

faq_plan.q: What should an employee personal information form include?
faq_plan.a: An employee personal information form should include the employee's legal name, date of birth, mailing address, and emergency contact, plus job title and start date. A volunteer form asks for much of the same contact information, without the job title or start date. With Emergent, each employee's answers go to a database you own, where HR can look anyone up by name.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries and printable PDFs (Jotform, Formplus, Zoho Forms, TemplateLab, Template.net, Scribd, Pinterest, a lab HR PDF). Each hands over a blank sheet of name, address, and date-of-birth boxes and stops. This page shows what happens to the details after someone fills them in, in four places a searcher will recognize: a school collecting teacher records before the year starts, a freight company handling a driver's change of address, a senior center turning a stack of paper forms into records, and an events agency whose on-call servers fill the form on a phone. The FAQ covers the definition, the PII short form, email sharing, format, samples, templates, teachers, employees, and change forms.
